2026-12-17.title: Thursday after the Sunday of the Apparition to St Joseph · Mar Rabbula
readings: The God of peace will crush Satan
You will know them by their fruits
2026-12-17.alt: Mar Rabbula, Bishop of Edessa (died around 436), remembered in the Syriac tradition. The Twenty-Five Days' Fast before Yaldo continues.
2026-12-17.verse: Thus you will know them by their fruits.
theo: At the end of Romans Paul warns against those who cause dissensions and offences, serving “their own appetites” and deceiving the simple with smooth talk. He wants the Romans to be “wise in what is good and guileless in what is evil.” And then a promise that echoes Genesis: “The God of peace will shortly crush Satan under your feet.” The child born of the woman will strike the serpent's head; his victory becomes ours.

Jesus warns against false prophets who come in sheep's clothing. How do we recognise them? Not by their eloquence or their claims, but by their fruits: a good tree bears good fruit, a bad tree bad fruit. “Thus you will know them by their fruits.” The same test applies to us. In these last days of the fast we ask whether our lives bear the fruits of Christ: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness.
outline: How do you recognise a true teacher?

altar: At the Holy Qurbono we receive the true fruit of the tree of life, Christ himself, who makes us good trees.

2026-12-17.question: What fruit does my life bear?

family.explain: Jesus says we know a tree by its fruit. Good people show their goodness by what they do.
family.intention: We pray that our family may bear good fruit.
family.ask: Ask: “What good fruit did each of us bear this week?”

pm.open: God of peace, you will crush evil under our feet. As we gather, keep us faithful to the teaching we have received and make us bear good fruit. Amen.
share: Paul warns against those who cause divisions (Romans 16:17). Am I a source of unity or division?
Jesus says: you will know them by their fruits (Matthew 7:16). What fruit does my faith bear?
Which voices do I listen to about God, and are they trustworthy?
pm.resp: Lord, make us good trees bearing good fruit.
interc: For the Church, that she may remain united in the true faith.
For those deceived by false teachers, that they may find the truth.
For the bishops of our Church, that they may guard the flock.
For those who cause division, that they may be converted.
For our families, that they may bear good fruit.
pm.close: Lord God, you promised to crush the serpent's head. Keep us in the true faith, protect us from deception, and make our lives fruitful in love. Amen.

illus: A family in Kottayam was drawn into a group that promised miracles in exchange for large donations. The fruits were debt and quarrels. Their parish priest gently helped them return. The father said: “I learnt to look at the fruits, not the noise.”

homily: Dear friends, St Paul ends his letter to the Romans with a warning: keep an eye on those who cause dissensions and offences, in opposition to the teaching that you have learned; avoid them. By smooth talk and flattery they deceive the hearts of the simple-minded (Romans 16:17–18).

Then he gives a beautiful promise: the God of peace will shortly crush Satan under your feet (Romans 16:20). This recalls the first promise of salvation in Genesis, that the offspring of the woman would crush the serpent's head. At Yaldo that promise begins to be fulfilled.

In the Gospel Jesus says: beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep's clothing but inwardly are ravenous wolves. You will know them by their fruits. Every good tree bears good fruit, but the bad tree bears bad fruit (Matthew 7:15–17).

Today many voices claim to speak for God: on television, on social media, in new movements. Some bring division, fear and money-making. Jesus gives a simple test: look at the fruits. Do they lead to humility, charity, unity with the Church, and holiness of life?
The test applies to us too. What fruit does my faith bear? Patience at home, honesty at work, generosity to the poor, faithfulness in prayer? A good tree is known not by its leaves but by its fruit.

During the last days of the fast, let us hold fast to the faith we received from the Church, avoid what divides, and ask God to make us good trees. The God of peace will crush evil under our feet. Amen.
kids: Children, a good tree gives good fruit. Be a good tree: do good things today!

intro: Theme: “You will know them by their fruits.”
Discernment and the victory of the God of peace.

sub: Jeremiah warned of prophets speaking their own visions.
q: Thus says the LORD of hosts: Do not listen to the words of the prophets who prophesy to you; they are deluding you. They speak visions of their own minds, not from the mouth of the LORD.
Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep's clothing but inwardly are ravenous wolves.

sub: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom.
Be wise in good, guileless in evil.
q: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom, and the knowledge of the Holy One is insight.
For while your obedience is known to all, so that I rejoice over you, I want you to be wise in what is good and guileless in what is evil.

sub: The psalm: you will trample the serpent.

q: You will tread on the lion and the adder, the young lion and the serpent you will trample under foot.
The God of peace will shortly crush Satan under your feet. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.

concl: The God of peace is stronger than evil.
